title: Prove the sharp first-extension degree for regular pencils (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove the exact worst-case least extension degree admitting an invertible projective slice of a regular n-by-n matrix pencil over every finite field F_q:

```text
U_q(d) = 1 + sum(k=1..d) k I_q(k)
E_q(n) = min { d >= 1 : n < U_q(d) }
I_q(k) = number of monic irreducible degree-k polynomials over F_q
```

Claim type: scoped all-prime-power, all-dimension proof with exact finite corroboration. A companion-block pencil attains every worst-case first degree. U_q(d) is the sharp minimum dimension for failure over every extension degree through d. No new kappa is claimed.

The new step counts the union of projective points across extension degrees, rather than using the size of one prescribed extension. It supplies an exact field-normalization obstruction for algebraic native-interface exploration. This is an original side question; predecessor decomposition and determinant-character results are cited context, not audited deliverables.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Ali Romman / #5689 for the regular-pencil/no-base-slice interface and projective-point family, #5692/#5712 for later decomposition/transport, apoursh / #5672, Nick Petalas / #5250, David Ganz's tensor-atlas lineage, and the retained classical Kronecker, companion and finite-field work. Frobenius, irreducible counts and root counting are classical; global literature priority is unclaimed.

## Evidence

The written proof gives the universal upper bound and matching literal construction. A self-contained checker enumerates 1,707 nonzero homogeneous forms over F2/F3/F4/F5, comparing projective-point evaluation with polynomial divisibility. It constructs 18 threshold/padded pencils and checks 828 literal determinants, with seven named semantic controls and six malformed-input rejections. No predecessor executable is imported.

Both warning-strict direct commands pass locally in about 0.15 seconds each. The registered launcher passes both checks in about 0.60 seconds total, well below their individual 120-second limits. Normal and optimized receipts agree. Final committed-byte/mode and declared-source-history checks pass at `e9548573ead05bbecaaa6e194f9f8298d9a6923a` for all seven package files. Official export and input-coverage integrity pass. Normal and optimized replay from the read-only export with empty PATH pass in about 0.16 seconds each, preserve every byte/mode, and produce the same generated source-hash receipt.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The theorem requires a square regular pencil and concerns the first successful extension, which may depend on the pencil. It does not assert monotonicity in integer extension degree. Singular or rectangular pencils have no such guarantee. The executable covers only q=2,3,4,5 and its displayed bounded domains; arbitrary fields/dimensions rest on the written proof.

No efficient general witness finder, original-field equivalence/SL descent, native realization, coefficient-preparation tariff, restored dirty-input protocol, physical caller or complete recursive invoice is supplied. All five selected framework assumptions remain. No native supplier replay, selected scientific cold replay, Lean or Docker build was run. No registered local check is deferred to CI. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. The selected frontier is unchanged.

## Open next questions

- Construct a first-success field and invertible slice efficiently from raw matrices without enumerating all irreducibles through the threshold. Start with the homogeneous determinant and its absent irreducible factors; efficient witness search and full arithmetic cost remain open.
- Bind an extension-slice normalization to one fully priced native producer/consumer, including field descent, coefficient maps and dirty restoration. No physical implementation or favorable complete invoice is established here.

No follow-on is attempted or reserved.

## Related open work

- #6422 studies the least intermediate subfield supporting determinant-norm witnesses. It does not compute this first successful extension degree for pencil slices; the field-selection quantities and witness contracts differ.
- #2985 appeared in the open pencil search but studies E8 one-sided residue closures, rather than regular finite-field pencil normalization. No numerical comparison applies.

The completion refresh listed all eleven open contributions on this account created since the advance CLAIM at `2026-11-02T23:14:51Z`, including this PR. The other ten study different objects or quantities; none computes this regular-pencil slice threshold, and no conflicting overlapping value was identified. This comparison used PR text without extra scientific replay.

Merged #5689/#5692/#5712 supply the pencil-interface context. Merged #6309 optimizes raw-pencil matrix products and does not study this extension threshold. No extra computation rechecked those results.
